title: bim-bench: AIは BIM モデルの空間構造をどこまで読めるか
description:
A benchmark measuring how far large language models can read the spatial structure of a building from IFC: the site-building-storey-space hierarchy, which elements belong to which storey, and the quantities attached to them.

IFC is a graph, not a drawing, so the questions have exact answers that a parser can confirm. The corpus is buildingSMART's own Sample-Test-Files, published under CC BY 4.0 and bundled here with attribution.

Principal finding: accuracy and cost separate in opposite directions. Arm B (no code execution) reached 235/255 on element attribution at 372k tokens and 36 minutes; arm C (Python permitted) reached 255/255 at 99k tokens and 9 minutes — better on every axis at roughly a quarter of the cost. Arm C additionally declined to trust a quantity field it could not verify, and derived the volumes independently.

IFC に入っている空間構造・要素の所属・数量を読み取る能力を測る。コード実行を許した腕が、点数でもコストでも上回った。

Part of the AI Practical Reach Index, a series applying one common yardstick across Japanese professional domains.
